name: ApoB / ApoA-I ratio
aliases: Apolipoprotein B to apolipoprotein A1 ratio
rangeNote: The app records the ratio reported by the laboratory; it never silently computes it from separate results. There is no universal app range: the laboratory's range is used when supplied, and interpretation depends on the individual ApoB and ApoA-I results and overall heart risk.
summary: This is apolipoprotein B (ApoB) divided by apolipoprotein A-I (ApoA-I), with both proteins expressed in the same mass units. ApoB reflects the number of particles that can contribute to artery plaque, while ApoA-I is the main protein in high-density lipoprotein (HDL). A higher ratio is associated with higher heart attack risk, but it is not a diagnosis or a replacement for looking at both proteins separately.

high.meaning: A higher ratio means more ApoB relative to ApoA-I. It can reflect high ApoB, low ApoA-I, or both; discuss a result above the laboratory's range with your doctor in the context of the separate results and other heart risk factors.
commonCauses: Higher ApoB, including inherited lipid patterns or insulin resistance
Lower ApoA-I during inflammation or acute illness
A combination of higher ApoB and lower ApoA-I

low.meaning: A lower ratio is generally associated with lower heart attack risk, but a high ApoA-I can make the ratio low even when ApoB is raised. It does not prove that the particle burden is low or that raising ApoA-I would prevent disease; discuss an unexpectedly low result with your doctor.
commonCauses: Lower ApoB, for example during cholesterol-lowering treatment
A combination of lower ApoB and higher ApoA-I
